conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during this stay. Can you tell me about the pain you're having?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s back, same as before—sharp pain in my upper belly, going to the left side. Feels just like my last flare-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Any nausea or vomiting this time?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Just at the start, but not now. I’ve been passing gas and having loose stools, so that’s good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That helps rule out a blockage. You mentioned you’ve had blood in your urine recently?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, a few days ago, but it went away on its own. No burning or urgency now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good to know. We’ll check a urine test just in case, but since it resolved, it may not be urgent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Is this another pancreatitis flare?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It looks that way. Your CT scan shows changes consistent with chronic pancreatitis—calcifications and atrophy of the pancreas.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So no blockage?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No sign of obstruction. There are some air-fluid levels, but they’re nonspecific—could be from slowed bowel movement due to pain or meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t been eating much because of the pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. We’ll keep you NPO for now—no food by mouth—to let your pancreas rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Again? How long will that be?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Usually 24 to 48 hours. We’ll give you IV fluids and pain meds. Once the pain settles, we’ll start you on clear liquids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’ve been using Dilaudid at home. Is that still okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re giving IV Dilaudid now for better control. Once you’re eating, we’ll switch back to oral.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my diabetes meds? I take metformin and insulin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood sugar has been low—between 60 and 90—because you’re not eating. We’ve held both the insulin and metformin for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I restart them when I get home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Only when you’re eating regularly again and your sugars are above 130. We’ll write that in your discharge instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How’s the pain today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. Still there, but not as intense. Can I try some food?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start with clear liquids—broth, apple juice—and see how you tolerate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Any chance this was something else, like a bowel blockage?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We were concerned at first, but the CT showed no obstruction. The bowel gas pattern is nonspecific, likely due to the flare-up and reduced intake.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my heart and lungs? The chest X-ray okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, chest X-ray was clear—no pneumonia, fluid, or free air. All stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve been feeling anxious with the pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I noticed you were tearful yesterday. As your pain improves, your mood seems better too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, it’s hard when the pain’s bad. I take duloxetine and lorazepam.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve continued your lorazepam, and we’re adjusting your duloxetine dose down to 30 mg daily for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Why lower it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just to minimize side effects while you’re recovering. You can discuss adjusting it back with your psychiatrist if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well. Pain is much improved, and you’ve tolerated a regular diet since yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I can go home today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We’re discharging you with a few days of oral Dilaudid for pain, and Miralax to prevent constipation from the pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my pancreas enzymes?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, continue taking three capsules with meals. Also keep up the omeprazole and low-fat diet to reduce strain on your pancreas.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll follow up with my GI doctor?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and your primary care provider to monitor your blood sugars and restart your diabetes meds when appropriate.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks, doctor. I’ll avoid alcohol and driving while on the Dilaudid.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Call us if the pain worsens or you develop fever, vomiting, or dark urine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Appreciate the care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. Get some rest and follow the instructions closely.
